title: 2.11/s3: GET after PUT includes chunk-signature
body:
I have set up a SeaweedFS cluster with the following components:

3x master (`weed master -mdir=/data -volumePreallocate -volumeSizeLimitMB=1024 -ip=10.132.0.xx -mdir=/data -peers=10.132.0.58:9333,10.132.0.60:9333,10.132.0.57:9333`)
4x volume (`weed volume -dir=/data -max=0 -ip=10.132.0.xx -mserver=10.132.0.58:9333,10.132.0.60:9333,10.132.0.57:9333 -dataCenter=dc -rack=rack -dir=/data`)
4x filer+s3 (`weed filer -ip=10.132.0.xx -master=10.132.0.58:9333,10.132.0.60:9333,10.132.0.57:9333 -peers=10.132.0.58:8888,10.132.0.60:8888,10.132.0.57:8888,10.132.0.56:8888 -s3`)

The deployment is dockerized (using the `chrislusf/seaweedfs:dev` Docker image).

The cluster is deployed on four GCE n2-standard-8 instances (8 vCPUs, 32 GB RAM) with local NVMe attached as storage, which is formatted with XFS and used to host the data of the volume container.

The filer is configured to use leveldb2 as filer store:

```
[leveldb2]
enabled = true
dir = "/data"
```

**Describe the bug**

When running a benchmark using [warp](https://github.com/minio/warp), warp reports the following error:

```
warp: <ERROR> unexpected download size. want:256, got:430                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
warp: <ERROR> unexpected download size. want:256, got:430                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
warp: <ERROR> unexpected download size. want:256, got:430
```

A simple way to reproduce this is to run `warp` in `get` mode for a short time:

```
warp get --host instance-seaweedfs-1 --access-key x --secret-key x --concurrent 1 --obj.size 256B --objects 2 --duration 1s
```

Checking via `tcpdump` the following requests are exchanged:

The response to the GET request includes `chunk-signature` elements which increase the expected size from 256 bytes to 430 bytes.

**System Setup**
- Linux instance-seaweedfs-2 5.4.0-1029-gcp #31-Ubuntu SMP Wed Oct 21 19:38:01 UTC 2020 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- `version 30GB 2.11 5f3546a6 linux amd64`
- `filer.toml`:

```
# A sample TOML config file for SeaweedFS filer store
# Used with "weed filer" or "weed server -filer"
# Put this file to one of the location, with descending priority
#    ./filer.toml

####################################################

# directories under this folder will be automatically creating a separate bucket
buckets_folder = "/buckets"
buckets_fsync = [          # a list of buckets with all write requests fsync=true
        "important_bucket",
        "should_always_fsync",
]

####################################################
# The following are filer store options
####################################################

# local on disk, mostly for simple single-machine setup, fairly scalable
# faster than previous leveldb, recommended.

enabled = false

password = ""

[postgres] # or cockroachdb
# CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS filemeta (
#   dirhash     BIGINT,
#   name        VARCHAR(65535),
#   directory   VARCHAR(65535),
#   meta        bytea,
#   PRIMARY KEY (dirhash, name)
# );
enabled = false

port = 5432
username = "postgres"
password = ""

# CREATE TABLE filemeta (
#    directory varchar,
#    name varchar,
#    meta blob,
#    PRIMARY KEY (directory, name)
# ) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (name ASC);

    "localhost:30001",
    "localhost:30002",
    "localhost:30003",
    "localhost:30004",
    "localhost:30005",
    "localhost:30006",
]
password = ""
# allows reads from slave servers or the master, but all writes still go to the master
readOnly = true
# automatically use the closest Redis server for reads
routeByLatency = true

[etcd]
enabled = false
servers = ""
timeout = "3s"

[mongodb]
enabled = false
uri = "mongodb://localhost:27017"
option_pool_size = 0
database = "seaweedfs"

[elastic7]

servers = [
    "http://localhost1:9200",
    "http://localhost2:9200",
    "http://localhost3:9200",

healthcheck_enabled = false
# increase the value is recommend, be sure the value in Elastic is greater or equal here
index.max_result_window = 10000
```

**Expected behavior**
The response to the GET request is expected not to contain `chunk-signature` elements so that the `warp` benchmark works with seaweedfs as it already does with minio and ceph.
